 Dengue cases reported to decrease in Jalisco
 Dengue cases reported to decrease in Jalisco 
 In comparison to 2025, when more than 300 cases were recorded, only 215 confirmed cases have been reported this year. 
 Audio from the Press Conference 32.11 MB 
 Dengue fever in Jalisco has decreased compared to last year, with 215 confirmed cases reported , representing a drop of more than 86 percent compared to 2025 , when 317 cases were recorded . 
 This decrease in confirmed cases is attributed to the preventive actions of the population and the various government bodies, and it is expected that if these initiatives are strengthened from schools and homes the advance of dengue in Jalisco will continue to decline. 
 “Dengue is a virus that has an active epidemiological situation every year; in some years it is more active than in others, but it always has a constant and continuous epidemiological prevalence,” stated Dr. Roberto Miguel Damián Negrete, director of the Health division of  Centro Universitario de Tlajomulco (CUTlajomulco) . 
 The specialist explained that dengue is mainly transmitted by the female Aedes aegypti mosquito; this insect can infect a person with any of the four serotypes of the dengue virus, and there is a possibility that after being infected by the virus, a second infection may be more severe than the first. 
 Some symptoms of classic dengue fever include fever above 39 or 40 degrees Celsius , severe headaches, as well as pain behind the eyes and throughout the body . However, there is also severe dengue, which requires hospitalization and is characterized by intense abdominal pain, vomiting, and possible bleeding . 
 “This situation does put patients’ lives at risk; for this reason, if symptoms exist, it is imperative and extremely necessary that they go to hospitals to confirm the disease, which is diagnosed with a blood test within the first five days,” he said. 
 Dr. Laura Karina Salas Salazar, head of the Healthy Living and Health Promotion Department at CUTlajomulco, stated that as of epidemiological week 41, 859 cases of dengue fever have been recorded in Mexico , placing Jalisco among the top 13 states with the most confirmed cases. “Jalisco continues to be a state that, due to its climate and population density, is always under strict epidemiological surveillance,” she affirmed. 
 He recalled that, according to data from the Jalisco Development Indicators Monitoring (Mide) , 941 cases of dengue were reported in 2023; 20,907 cases in 2024; 2,317 were registered in 2025; and this year, up to September 30, 215 had been counted. 
 They reiterate their commitment to implementing strategies against dengue. 
 To minimize the impact of this disease on the population, CUTlajomulco is working with the federal government to promote the 2026 Regional Dengue Forum on October 29th , which will address strategies to unify vector control protocols and define the public health agenda for the state. 
 “It was normally thought that dengue was a seasonal disease and that it only affected people during rainy times, but recent years have shown us that the disease also prevails in the winter season ,” warned Dr. Yordi Raúl Portillo Montes, leader of Management and Rectorate in Health of Jalisco. 
 Given this particular situation, he stressed that prevention strategies must be strengthened throughout the year, and the forum is one of those efforts to reduce the incidence of this disease in Jalisco. 
 He explained that in other regional forums, strategies such as intensive community cleanup, placement of larvicide in water containers, and fumigation of strategic areas have been addressed ; work has also been done to update first and second level medical personnel in the detection of warning signs, and ovitraps have been placed to identify the presence of virus serotypes early. 
 These strategies must be added to the actions of citizens to prevent the spread of the mosquito that transmits dengue, said Dr. Juan Antonio Santoscoy Aceves, state coordinator of the National Public Health Service, who stressed that these measures must also reach parents, teachers, community leaders and other people who influence society. 
 The 2026 Regional Dengue Forum will take place on October 29th , from 9:00 a.m. to 13:00 p.m., at CUTlajomulco. Anyone interested in promoting dengue prevention is welcome to participate; no prior registration is required.
